paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as a student of R' Yonah. At the beginning of Yevamot chapter 9 he asks R' Yonah a question, and in 8:6, according to Hyman, he reports R' Yonah. At the beginning of Kilayim chapter 9: Rabbi Nicha bar Savah; Rabbi Yochanan (Hyman says it should read Rabbi Yose), in Rabbi Zeira's name.

notes.text: The final Kilayim passage juxtaposes Nicha and Yochanan without spelling out their link. Hyman proposes Yose for Yochanan; the Sava/Savah spelling difference is retained.

The saved whole Guggenheimer Kilayim9 opening scalar has full Rabbi Nicha bar Savah, Rabbi Yochanan, in Rabbi Zeira’s name, without an explicit connector between the first two. Hyman’s should-read Rabbi Yose remains his conjecture, not an adopted primary reading. Heading Sava and cited Savah remain different spellings. The Yevamot study/report notices are Hyman’s uninspected citations this wake; their Yonah title stays R'. No new genealogical or intermediate transmission link is invented.

Yevamot 9:1 records Nicha bar Sava asking Rabbi Yonah a question. In 8:6, Nicha is called the son of Rabbi Sava, and his name stands before Rabbi Yonah reporting in the name of Rav Hamnuna. Kilayim 9:1 likewise places Nicha bar Savah before Rabbi Yochanan in a report in the name of Rabbi Zeira. Neither chain spells out the link between its first two names. Hyman proposes Yose for Yochanan in Kilayim.
